Implement `src/index.js` so it exports `TableError`, `stringWidth`, `wrapCell`, `padCell` and `formatTable`. `TableError` extends `Error`, sets `name` to `'TableError'`, carries a `code` string, and is constructed as `(code, message)`. Everything below measures text in terminal columns, never in code units, so iterate by code point.

`stringWidth(text)` returns the column count of a string, throwing `'BAD_CELL'` with message `cell must be a string` for a non-string. A code point below U+0020, U+007F, any of U+200B, U+200C, U+200D and U+FEFF, or anything in U+0300 to U+036F counts as 0 columns. A code point in any of these inclusive ranges counts as 2 columns: U+1100-U+115F, U+2E80-U+303E, U+3041-U+33FF, U+3400-U+4DBF, U+4E00-U+9FFF, U+A000-U+A4CF, U+AC00-U+D7A3, U+F900-U+FAFF, U+FE10-U+FE19, U+FE30-U+FE6F, U+FF00-U+FF60, U+FFE0-U+FFE6, U+1F300-U+1F64F, U+1F900-U+1F9FF, U+20000-U+2FFFD and U+30000-U+3FFFD. Everything else counts as 1.

`wrapCell(text, width)` returns the lines a cell occupies in a column of `width` columns, always at least one line, and never a line wider than `width`. `width` must be an integer of at least 1 (`'BAD_WIDTH'`, `width must be a positive integer`) and `text` must be a string (`'BAD_CELL'`, `cell must be a string`). The text is first split on newlines and each piece wrapped on its own, so an empty piece contributes one empty line. Within a piece, runs of one or more spaces separate words and collapse to a single space; leading and trailing spaces disappear, and a piece with no words yields one empty line. A word wider than the column is broken greedily into chunks of at most `width` columns, so a 2-column character that would straddle the edge starts the next chunk and leaves the previous one a column short; a single character wider than the whole column throws `'UNWRAPPABLE'` with message `character is wider than the column`. Words and chunks are then packed greedily, one space between neighbours on the same line, starting a new line whenever the next word would push the line past `width`.

`padCell(text, width, align)` pads one already-fitting line to exactly `width` columns, with `align` defaulting to `'left'` and also accepting `'right'` and `'center'`; centring puts the smaller half of the padding on the left. It throws `'BAD_CELL'` for a non-string, `'BAD_WIDTH'` with message `width must be a positive integer` for a bad width, `'BAD_ALIGN'` with message `unknown alignment: <align>` for anything else, and `'CELL_TOO_WIDE'` with message `content is wider than the column` when the text does not fit. `formatTable(rows, options)` renders `rows`, an array of arrays of strings, using `options.widths` (an array of positive integers, one per column), the optional `options.align` (one alignment per column, all `'left'` by default) and the optional boolean `options.header`. Validation runs in this order, each failure throwing immediately: `options` must be a non-null object (`'BAD_OPTIONS'`, `options must be an object`); `widths` must be a non-empty array of positive integers (`'BAD_WIDTH'`, `widths must be a non-empty array of positive integers`); `align`, when given, must be an array of the same length (`'BAD_ALIGN'`, `align must have <n> entries`) holding known alignments (`'BAD_ALIGN'`, `unknown alignment: <value>`); `rows` must be an array (`'BAD_ROWS'`, `rows must be an array`); and each row, in order, must have one cell per column (`'BAD_ROW_LENGTH'`, `row <i> has <n> cells, expected <m>`, counting a non-array row as 0 cells) with every cell a string (`'BAD_CELL'`, `cell at row <i>, column <j> is not a string`). No rows renders the empty string. Otherwise every cell is wrapped to its column, a row occupies as many lines as its tallest cell with the shorter cells padded out with blanks, and the cells of one line are padded and joined with ` | `. When `header` is true a rule of hyphens per column joined with `-+-` follows the first row. Lines are joined with newlines, with no trailing newline, and every line of the result has the same display width. Change only files under src/.
